method: Primary programme material and selected technical sections. All future factory prices, freight surcharges, localization shares and technology bundles are disclosed study assumptions. No external datasets or full publications are redistributed.

sources.title: Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems for Lunar Surface Applications
sources.reading_scope: PDF text, presentation pages on architecture, long-duration mass comparisons, balance of plant and thermal control (PDF pages 3–9).
sources.supports: Long-duration regenerative storage, approximately half round-trip efficiency and the importance of complete fluid and thermal hardware.
sources.limit: Development presentation; not a lunar utility demonstration or price quotation.

sources.title: On the Moon to Stay: Challenges Presented to Power Distribution by Sustained Operations on the Lunar Surface
sources.reading_scope: PDF text, overview pages on illumination, photovoltaic, regenerative and fission options (PDF pages 4–12).
sources.supports: Ordinary lunar nights and substantial polar interruptions; multiple supply technologies under development.
sources.limit: Dated development targets, not a surveyed site profile or 2026 delivered hardware.

sources.title: NASA Regenerative Fuel Cell Testing
sources.reading_scope: Article body describing 2025 tests and planned 2026 integrated work.
sources.limit: Planned closed-loop and environmental testing are not reported as completed qualification.

sources.title: A Deployable 40 kWe Lunar Fission Surface Power Concept
sources.reading_scope: PDF text, mass table and conversion system discussion, PDF pages 3–4.
sources.supports: Concept mass 10046 kg for power, controls and cable at 40 kW; separate mobility 2080 kg; limited conversion efficiency.
sources.limit: Concept with margins, not flight hardware. Mobility is separate; the middle 50 kg/kW assumption is not drawn from this design.

sources.title: Multi-Megawatt Gas Turbine Power Systems for Lunar Colonies
sources.reading_scope: Abstract and introduction, conversion discussion and Table 2 (PDF pages 5–6 and 11–13); NTRS publication metadata.
sources.supports: Calculated 43170 kg lunar concept at 10 MWe; scale and conversion design change specific mass. Introduction identifies difficult high-temperature heat storage and retrieval as an objection to regolith thermal storage.
sources.limit: Lunar power concept with instrument shielding and unresolved development issues, not a complete qualified inhabited-site installation. Its thermal-storage judgment is an engineering assessment, not a demonstration that later designs cannot work.

sources.title: Analysis of lunar regolith thermal energy storage
sources.reading_scope: NTRS abstract and publication metadata; the full paper was not reviewed for this comparison.
sources.supports: Analytical study of heat retention, cylindrical and spherical geometries and repeated lunar cycles.
sources.limit: Thermal behavior in a mathematical model does not establish recoverable electric output, the assumed 80% retention or lightweight containment.

sources.title: Sunlight Extracts Oxygen From Regolith Using Solar Chemistry
sources.reading_scope: Agency account of the CaRD integrated concentrator, reactor and controls; read with the enclosed feasibility source review.
sources.supports: Direct solar process heat and reported carbon-monoxide production support a process-specific alternative to all-electric heating.
sources.limit: Prototype result, not continuous production at the programme scale or a substitute for all electrical loads.

sources.title: Space Solar Power Project Ends First In-Space Mission with Successes and Lessons
sources.reading_scope: Caltech mission account, transfer demonstrations and hardware lessons; read with the enclosed feasibility source review.
sources.supports: Demonstrated wireless transfer and lessons about space deployment and thermal performance.
sources.limit: No utility-scale delivered power, kilometre aperture qualification or cost established.
